clue.text: Solar ray?

parts.note: a beam of light coming from our star, read straight as a plain description

explanation.surface: A short query about light from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of sunlight is literally a ray from the sun.

clue.text: Cross woman with design leader? That is astute!

parts.note: a shrew is a bad-tempered, scolding woman

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of design

explanation.surface: Someone admires a bad-tempered woman who also heads up the design team.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone sharp-witted and quick to judge a situation well.

clue.text: Table-linen in northern primate's home?

parts.note: an apery is a place where apes are kept, a home for primates

explanation.surface: Wondering what tablecloths are found in the house of a northern ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is an old word for household linen, especially cloths and napkins for the dining table.

clue.text: Mustering strangely silent soldiers onto square

indicators.note: strangely tells us the word silent is rearranged into an odd order

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for soldiers, the rank and file
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Troops falling quietly into line on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges SILENT to ENLIST; MEN and T then follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlistment is the signing up of recruits, a mustering of people into service.

clue.text: Virile, some say, to use speed of sound approaching round roundabout?

indicators.note: approaching places the first piece just before the next one in the answer

parts.note: Mach 1 is the speed of sound, so Mach names it
a roundabout is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A whimsical picture of a speeding vehicle nearing a circular road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: MACH is the unit for the speed of sound; a roundabout is a British circular road junction, shaped like O.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes an aggressively masculine, manly attitude, which some would call virile.

clue.text: Floats about at mouth of Mersey

definitions.text: Floats about at mouth of Mersey

indicators.note: about signals the word Floats is turned around and rearranged
the mouth of a river is where it starts its exit, here the opening letter of Mersey

explanation.surface: Debris drifting where the river Mersey meets the sea at Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges FLOATS to FLOTSA, then M from 'mouth of Mersey'. The Mersey is the river at Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is wreckage or rubbish found floating on the water, exactly what drifts at a river estuary.

clue.text: Front part smack into trailer

parts.note: the fore is the front part, as of a ship
a smack is a slight flavour or taste of something

explanation.surface: Someone slaps a lorry's trailer on the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer gives a preview, an early sample of what is to come.

clue.text: Frank old writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is described as an elderly author.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and open both mean candid, hiding nothing.

clue.text: Dagger in the heel

definitions.meaning: a short slim knife for stabbing
a tall thin heel on a woman's shoe

explanation.surface: A knife concealed in the heel of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a slender blade and a high narrow shoe heel named after it.

clue.text: These characters have sums taken from them

definitions.text: These characters have sums taken from them

parts.words: These characters have sums taken from them
parts.note: reads like people robbed of money, but means numbers from which other numbers are subtracted

explanation.surface: People who have had money taken from them.
explanation.definitionFit: In subtraction, the number you take another away from has this mathematical name.

clue.text: Drive back from Winder -mere, pelting

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Being driven back from Windermere in pelting rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Windermere is a lake in England's Lake District; the hyphen splitting it lets the answer straddle the break.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to force it back.

clue.text: Like the philosopher he thought he was?

definitions.text: Like the philosopher he thought he was?

parts.words: Like the philosopher he thought he was?
parts.note: alludes to Descartes's maxim I think therefore I am: he thought, so he was

explanation.surface: A wry question about a thinker's self-image.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Descartes and his thought; his famous proof of existence came from thinking.

clue.text: Poet giving merit to the ordinary things we say

parts.note: words are what we speak in everyday talk
worth is merit or value

explanation.surface: A poet who gives value to plain everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: William Wordsworth was an English Romantic poet who championed ordinary language in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was a leading English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Top player said to give in

indicators.note: said tells us we want a word pronounced like the one given

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: A leading sportsman is reported to have surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to yield or surrender something to another.

clue.text: Big banker experiments with commercial enterprises

parts.note: a river has banks, so a big banker is a large river, the Indus
tries are attempts or experiments

explanation.surface: A powerful financier trialling business ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big banker' suggests a financier, but a river has banks; the Indus is a great river of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Industries are branches of trade or manufacturing, kinds of business activity.

clue.text: Predominates, perhaps, like one mimicked

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word given is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone dominating a scene by mimicking another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PREDOMINATES; 'like one' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mimicked is to be imitated, copied in voice or manner.

clue.text: Extravagant garnish

definitions.meaning: a verb: to decorate or embellish

explanation.surface: A showy decoration on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means ornate; as a verb it means to add detail and decoration.

clue.text: Wake up in California, a musical?

indicators.note: in puts the waking word inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: rouse means wake someone up

explanation.surface: Waking up in California and asking if a musical is on.
explanation.walkthrough: Carousel is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is a famous Broadway musical by Rodgers and Hammerstein.

clue.text: Plainchant service?

parts.note: even means plain, flat or level
a chant is a kind of song

explanation.surface: Asking whether plainchant makes up a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plainchant' looks like one word but splits into Plain and chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.

clue.text: The edge of Wimbledon, love us, is superior!

parts.note: in tennis, played at Wimbledon, advantage is the edge after deuce
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis fan cheering that their side has the edge at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; 'advantage' is the score after deuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Being advantageous means being favourable, in a better position.

clue.text: Family tax

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or breed
a verb: to put under stress

explanation.surface: A family burdened by tax.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a lineage or breed and to overstretch, as taxing does.

clue.text: Squirm painfully and wither, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints the word wither can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something twisting in pain and drying up.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, as in pain.

clue.text: Sound from "Animal Farm", Orwell's first writing material

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Orwell's

parts.note: ink is the material used for writing

explanation.surface: Orwell's first draft of Animal Farm on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal Farm is Orwell's satire with farmyard animals, including pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt of a pig, a farm animal, the stars of Orwell's book.

clue.text: Smash price-motto of rival in business

indicators.note: smash suggests breaking the words price-motto into pieces and reforming them

explanation.surface: A firm attacking a rival's pricing slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is a rival firm in a market.

clue.text: Vibration felt in a peashooter

definitions.meaning: a regular beat felt in the wrist
a pea, a legume, is what a peashooter fires

explanation.surface: A shudder felt inside a toy pea-shooting tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a rhythmic heartbeat and also edible seeds such as peas and lentils.

clue.text: County no longer known

definitions.meaning: an English county in the south-east
an archaic past participle of ken, to know

explanation.surface: A county that has faded from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English county and an old form meaning recognised.

clue.text: Kind of defence not recommended for prison-building?

definitions.text: Kind of defence not recommended for prison-building?

parts.words: Kind of defence not recommended for prison-building?
parts.note: plays on the line ... do not a prison make, and on a stubborn blocking defence in sport

explanation.surface: A query about defensive tactics and jail construction.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stubborn blocking tactic, and the poem says such masonry does not make a jail.

clue.text: Spillage of paint is unsuitable

indicators.note: spillage suggests the word paint is spilt and its letters scattered

explanation.surface: Spilt paint is unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or not fitting.

clue.text: Opening in shelter for one who gets a gift by will

definitions.text: one who gets a gift by will

indicators.note: in puts the opening inside the shelter word

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A gap in a shelter for a beneficiary.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a legacy in a will.

clue.text: Substance or spirit of the French motorist

definitions.meaning: the core nature or concentrated extract of something

explanation.surface: Asking what a French driver is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: It means the core of a thing and is also the French word for petrol.
